summary: The appellant, a watchman employed since 1992, was terminated in 2002 without notice or due process under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. The Labour Court and Gujarat High Court (Single Judge) held the termination illegal and ordered reinstatement without backwages. The Division Bench set aside reinstatement and awarded ₹1 lakh as lumpsum compensation. The Supreme Court reversed, holding that the factual findings of illegal termination and procedural violations were unchallenged, and substitution of relief was unjustified given prolonged litigation caused by management. Reinstatement with continuity of service was restored.
legal_provisions_cited: Hindustan Tin Works (P) Ltd. v. Employees of M/s Hindustan Tin Works Pvt. Ltd. And Others, (1979) 2 SCC 80
Deepali Gundu Surwase v. Kranti Junior Adhyapak Mahavidyalaya and Others
final_judgment: The appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment setting aside reinstatement is set aside. The appellant shall be reinstated with continuity of service, in accordance with law.
